## Why This Is Asked
This tests end-to-end security gating in CI/CD for multi-service repos, including SBOM, licenses, attestations, and drift.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM (SPDX), whitelisted licenses, transitive dependencies
- Sigstore attestations, cosign
- OPA policies and policy-as-code
- CI workflow integration and fail interpretation

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: syft dir:. -o json> sbom.json
      - run: cosign verify <image>
      - run: opa eval --data policy.rego --input sbom.json
```

- How would you test the policy drift detection?
- Which metrics indicate gates are too strict or too lenient?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests advanced policy enforcement for image provenance in multi-cloud Kubernetes deployments, including runtime verification via canary tracing.

## Key Concepts
- OPA/ Gatekeeper policies for image provenance
- Docker image digests and container labels
- Canary tests and distribution across clouds
- End-to-end tracing with OTLP and trace-id linkage

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal Deployment manifest snippet
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-service
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-service
        data_version: v1.2.3
        model_version: v0.9.7
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: feature
        image: registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...
        imagePullPolicy: Always
```

```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions snippet (validation)
name: Validate Provenance
on: [push]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Inspect image for digest and labels
        run: |
          CONTAINER_IMG='registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...'
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' $CONTAINER_IMG | cut -d'@' -f2)
          LABELS=$(docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Labels}}' $CONTAINER_IMG)
          if [[ -z "$DIGEST" || "$LABELS" != *data_version* || "$LABELS" != *model_version* ]]; then
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Canary trace test
        run: |
          # pseudo-step: send request and verify OTLP trace propagates
          curl -sS http://feature-service.canary/health -H 'traceparent: 00-abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789-1234567812345678-01' >/dev/null
          # verification would query OTLP collector for trace-id
          echo 'Canary test passed'
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for high churn and lineage drift?
- What are the trade-offs of strict label enforcement vs. flexibility across teams?
- How would you simulate cross-cloud network latency in the gate?

```javascript
# Minimal Kyverno policy (YAML shown as JS block for readability)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: enforce-basic-security
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-psp

      any:
        - resources:
            kinds: [Namespace, Pod]
```

```javascript
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-pod

    securityContext:
      privileged: true
```
```javascript

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-pod
spec:
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to extend supply-chain security beyond images to function artifacts, and to integrate artifact attestations with a central provenance store in a multi-cloud serverless context.

- Cosign signing for containers and function artifacts
- Dependency attestations (dep-attestation) linked to a provenance store

## Code Example

```javascript
// Minimal pseudo workflow outline (Kubernetes-admission flow not shown)
name: Sign Artifacts and Gate
on: [push]
jobs:
  sign_and_gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Sign container image
        run: cosign sign ghcr.io/org/app:tag
      - name: Sign function artifact
        run: cosign sign artifacts/org/app-wheel-0.1.0-py3-none.whl
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft ghcr.io/org/app:tag -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
      - name: Rekor attestations
        run: cosign attest --timeout=300s
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement real-world security gates that combine image scanning, attestation, and policy enforcement in a scalable multi‑tenant environment.

- PR‑level gating and local verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Run Trivy SBOM
    run: trivy image --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json image:tag
  - name: Cosign sign SBOM
    run: cosign sign -key cosign.pub sbom.json
  - name: Rekor attestation
    run: cosign attest sbom.json --type sbom --format json
```

```yaml
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint

- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (ImageProvenanceAndSecurity)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: imageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package imageprovenance
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          some i
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
          image := container.image
          startswith(image, "registry.example.com/")
          not endswith(image, ":latest")
          some digest := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].imageDigest
          msg := "image must be from registry.example.com with digest"
        }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (ImageProvenanceConstraint)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
metadata:

spec:
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests end-to-end image provenance across multi-cloud GPU workloads, combining CI, runtime policies, and verification in real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, Cosign, Sigstore, reproducible builds
- Kubernetes admission control (Kyverno/OPA)
- Buildx/OCI digests and registry security
- GPU workload constraints and cross-cloud policy

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: build, sign, verify
name: BuildSignVerify
on: [push]
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up QEMU/Buildx
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          docker buildx create --use
          image=registry.example.com/project/image:${{ github.sha }}
          docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
            -t $image --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1 .
          cosign sign -key cosign.key $image
          docker push $image
      - name: Verify signature
        run: cosign verify -key cosign.pub $image
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-image
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: check-cosign-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    verifyImages:
    - image: registry.example.com/*
      pattern: "^.+$"
```

```yaml
# Sample failing manifest (unsigned image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: guest-deploy
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/project/image:unsigned

```

```yaml
# Sample passing manifest (signed image with digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-deploy
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        build.sha256: "abcdef123456..."
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/project/image:sha-abcdef
```
